source_roots.title: Blocking PD1 prevents T-cell-promoted fibrosis in myocardial infarction
source_roots.mechanism: PD1+ activated T cells drive CXCL9/CXCR3-dependent cardiac fibroblast activation and fibrosis, largely independent of fibroblast PD-L1.
interventions: PD1+ vs PD1- T-cell adoptive transfer
limitations: Article provides sample n only for selected panels; complete per-arm counts, effect-size extraction and individual animal-level tables not yet audited.
Anti-PD1 started around time of MI; delayed intervention after established mature scar is explicitly a future experiment.
Reduced scar or lower ACTA2/COL1A1/POSTN is not lineage-traced EXIT.
Authors explicitly note long-term checkpoint-inhibitor safety uncertain and possible immune-related myocarditis.

source_roots.title: Inhibition of Programmed Cell Death-1 in Cytotoxic CD8+ T Cells Exacerbates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Injury
source_roots.model: mouse pressure-overload transverse aortic constriction (TAC); human checkpoint therapy associated cardiac injury scRNA-seq resources
source_roots.mechanism: PD1 blockade/deletion promotes CXCR3+ cytotoxic CD8+ recruitment driven by fibroblast CXCL9/CXCL10, GZMB/perforin injury to cardiomyocyte mitochondrial complex I.
source_roots.effect_direction: PD1 blockade worsens pressure-overload cardiac injury/heart failure, opposite to reported post-MI fibrosis benefit in CHEN_MI_2026.
limitations: Distinct disease model, intervention context, immune cell subsets and readouts; not a direct same-model replication or formal logical contradiction.
Patient scRNA-seq Zenodo resource and GEO entries should be matched to exact assays before replay.
No evidence of therapeutic human MI safety/efficacy.

comparison.three_distinct_roots: Vargas Aguilar neonatal gamma-delta IL17A beneficial immune resolution; Chen adult MI activated PD1+ T-cell profibrotic axis; Wu TAC anti-PD1 adverse cytotoxic CXCR3+ CD8 T-cell axis.
comparison.core_constraint: The sign of PD1 immune intervention cannot be generalized across cardiac injury models. The same CXCL9/CXCR3 family may act in distinct source->target directions and cell subsets.
comparison.human_clinical_recommendation: NONE__anti-PD1 is a high-risk oncology immunotherapy class; no patient treatment inference from these animal experiments.

next_TOPA: Obtain GSE292863 bulk RNA-seq and GSE293489 scRNA-seq sample manifest, map exact animal IDs/MI timing and hash files; no cell-as-replicate inference.
Obtain GSE328788/GSE327655 and Zenodo Wu resources; verify assay/model linkage, independent sample n and provenance before cross-study comparisons.
Extract original source tables/figures for CHEN and WU, time-zero, dose, animal n, effect sizes, CI, and matching fibrosis and heart-function readouts.
Freeze MI versus TAC strata and immune-cell identity before testing effect sign; distinguish PD1+ T-cell subsets, IL17+ neonatal gamma-delta T cells, and cytotoxic CD8+ cells.
Search for delayed post-established-scar PD1/CXCR3 perturbation with lineage-resolved fibroblast fate and ECM clearance; absent this, maintain strict EXIT gate closed.
Never recommend anti-PD1 therapy for myocardial infarction based on animal findings; document myocarditis/cardiotoxicity and model-specific opposing effects.
